conventions: Rates are decimals. Bracket rows are [lowerBound, marginalRate]; the rate applies to state taxable income above lowerBound up to the next row. Amounts in USD. std.kind / exemption.kind: deduction = subtracted from income, credit = subtracted from tax, none = not available. start: federalAGI = state return begins with federal AGI; federalTaxable = begins with federal taxable income (the federal standard/itemized deduction is already reflected, so do not subtract std again); own = state defines its own gross income. Phase-outs are described in notes and the amounts shown are the base/maximum. Local tax rates are typical/indicative, not a per-locality table. Tax Foundation's table (published Feb 2025) was superseded where a state enacted 2025 changes or released final 2025 inflation figures; those states list the state source in crossCheckSources.

AL.name: Alabama

std.notes: Maximum amounts. Phase down for AGI above $25,999: single by $25 per $500 of AGI to a $2,500 floor; MFJ by $175 per $500 to a $5,000 floor.

AL.local: Occupational (wage) license taxes in some cities/counties, e.g. Birmingham 1%, Bessemer 1%, Gadsden 2%; most localities have none.
AL.notes: Federal income tax paid is deductible on the Alabama return. No 2025 rate change.

AZ.name: Arizona

std.notes: Tied to the federal standard deduction; ADOR's Feb 2026 update gives $15,750/$31,500 for 2025 (Tax Foundation's table showed the pre-OBBBA $15,000/$30,000). Non-itemizers can add 33% of charitable contributions.

exemption.notes: No personal exemption. Dependent credit $100 per dependent under 17 and $25 per dependent 17+; phases out above FAGI $200,000 single / $400,000 MFJ.

AZ.notes: Flat 2.5%, unchanged in 2025. HB 4168 (signed June 13, 2026) moved IRC conformity to Jan 1, 2026, with subtractions for the federal tips/overtime deductions from tax year 2025.

AR.name: Arkansas

std.notes: 2025 DFA instructions (Tax Foundation listed $2,410/$4,820).

exemption.notes: $29 personal tax credit per taxpayer, spouse and dependent.

AR.notes: Brackets are DFA's 2025 regular table for net income up to $94,700 (same for all filing statuses). Above $94,700 a bracket adjustment removes the lower brackets: from $97,801, tax = 3.9% x net income - $89.30 (about 2% on the first $4,700 and 3.9% above). Separate low-income tables give lower tax at low incomes. Top rate 3.9% since 2024, unchanged in 2025.

CA.name: California

std.notes: 2025 FTB indexed amounts (Tax Foundation showed 2024 amounts).

exemption.notes: Exemption credits are cut by $6 per credit for each $2,500 of federal AGI above $252,203 (single) / $504,411 (MFJ).

CA.notes: 2025 FTB brackets (Tax Foundation showed 2024). The rows at $1,000,000 add the 1% Behavioral Health Services Tax on taxable income over $1M (all filing statuses). The CA SDI payroll tax (no wage cap) is withheld separately and not included.

CO.name: Colorado

std.notes: Federal standard deduction, already included because Colorado starts from federal taxable income (federal 2025: $15,750/$31,500); do not subtract again. If AGI is over $300,000, std/itemized deductions above $12,000 (single) / $16,000 (MFJ) are added back.

CO.local: Occupational privilege taxes (flat monthly amounts on employees working in the city): Denver $5.75/mo, Aurora $2/mo, Greenwood Village $2/mo, Sheridan $3/mo, Glendale $5/mo.
CO.notes: Rate is back to 4.4% for 2025; the TABOR-triggered 4.25% applied to 2024 only.

CT.name: Connecticut

std.notes: No standard deduction.

exemption.notes: Personal exemption shrinks by $1,000 for each $1,000 of CT AGI above $30,000 (single) / $48,000 (MFJ), reaching zero at $45,000 / $72,000. Personal tax credits of 1%-75% of tax also apply at lower incomes.

CT.notes: Phase-outs: income in the 2% bracket is taxed at 4.5% once CT AGI exceeds $56,500 (single) / $100,500 (MFJ). Benefit recapture adds up to $3,150 (single) / $6,300 (MFJ) above $105,000 / $210,000, so very high earners pay about 6.99% on all income. No 2025 rate change.

DE.name: Delaware

exemption.notes: $110 personal credit per taxpayer, spouse and dependent.

DE.local: Wilmington 1.25% earned income (wage) tax on residents and on nonresidents working in the city.

GA.name: Georgia

exemption.notes: No personal exemption since 2024; $4,000 per dependent.

GA.notes: HB 111 (April 2025) cut the rate from 5.39% to 5.19%, retroactive to Jan 1, 2025. The Tax Foundation table still shows 5.39%.

HI.name: Hawaii

std.notes: Doubled for 2025 under Act 46 (2024).

HI.notes: Act 46 (2024) widened the brackets from 2025, with more bracket and std deduction steps scheduled for later years.

ID.name: Idaho

std.notes: Equal to the federal amount. Idaho adopted the 2025 federal (OBBBA) changes, including the tips, overtime, car-loan-interest and senior deductions.

exemption.notes: No personal exemptions. Idaho has a separate child tax credit.

ID.notes: HB 40 (March 2025) cut the rate from 5.695% to 5.3%, retroactive to Jan 1, 2025. The zero-rate band is indexed: $4,811 single / $9,622 MFJ (Tax Foundation shows the 2024 values $4,673/$9,346 at 5.695%).

std.notes: No standard deduction.

exemption.notes: Not allowed if AGI exceeds $250,000 (single) / $500,000 (MFJ).

IN.name: Indiana

std.notes: No standard deduction.

exemption.notes: Each qualifying dependent child gets another $1,500 ($3,000 in the first year a child is claimed).

IN.local: County income tax on all residents, about 0.5%-3.0% in 2025 (e.g. Marion County/Indianapolis 2.02%).
IN.notes: Rate cut from 3.05% to 3.0% for 2025. The IT-40 starting point follows the IRC as in effect on Jan 1, 2023.

IA.name: Iowa

std.notes: Federal standard deduction, already included because Iowa starts from federal taxable income with rolling IRC conformity (federal 2025: $15,750/$31,500); do not subtract again.

exemption.notes: $40 exemption credit per taxpayer, spouse and dependent.

IA.local: School district income surtaxes, levied as a percentage of the Iowa income tax and set by each district.
IA.notes: Graduated rates were replaced by a flat 3.8% for 2025.

KS.name: Kansas
KS.notes: Rates unchanged for 2025: the SB 269 revenue-triggered cut was not triggered (KDOR Notice 25-06).

KY.name: Kentucky

std.notes: $3,270 per person. A married-filing-joint return gets only one $3,270. Couples who file 'married filing separately on a combined return' get $3,270 each ($6,540), which most two-earner couples choose.

exemption.notes: No personal exemptions. Family Size Tax Credit for low incomes; personal tax credits for 65+/blind via Schedule ITC.

KY.local: Occupational license taxes on wages in most cities/counties, typically about 0.5%-2.5% combined (e.g. Louisville Metro about 2.2% for residents, Lexington-Fayette 2.25%), plus some school district taxes.

LA.name: Louisiana

std.notes: New for 2025; indexed from 2026.

exemption.notes: Act 11 (2024 3rd Extraordinary Session) repealed the extra $1,000 deductions for dependents, age 65+ and blind.

LA.notes: Graduated 1.85%/3.5%/4.25% replaced by a flat 3% for 2025. The old combined personal exemption-standard deduction was replaced by the std deduction above.

std.notes: Maine did not adopt the federal OBBBA increase for 2025. The std/itemized deduction phases out above Maine AGI of $100,000 (single) / $200,050 (MFJ).

exemption.notes: Personal exemption of $5,150 per person (a deduction) phases out above $333,450 (single) / $400,100 (MFJ). The dependent amount is a CREDIT: $305 per dependent, $610 per child under 6, phasing out at high incomes.

MD.name: Maryland

std.notes: Flat amounts from 2025, replacing the old 15%-of-income standard deduction with a minimum and maximum.

exemption.notes: $3,200 per exemption, reduced to $1,600 and then $800 as FAGI rises. It is $0 above $150,000 (single) / $200,000 (MFJ); the phase-out starts at $100,000 / $150,000.

MD.local: County/Baltimore City income tax on residents, 2.25% (Worcester) to 3.30% (Dorchester) in 2025; most counties 3.2%; Anne Arundel and Frederick use graduated local rates. Nonresidents pay a 2.25% special nonresident tax instead.
MD.notes: The 2025 Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act (effective tax year 2025) added 6.25% and 6.5% brackets, a flat std deduction, a 2% surtax on net capital gains when FAGI exceeds $350,000, and a 3.3% local rate cap. The Tax Foundation table predates these changes.

MA.name: Massachusetts

std.notes: No standard deduction.

MA.notes: Effectively a flat 5%, plus a 4% surtax (9% total) on income above $1,083,150 (the same threshold for joint filers). Short-term capital gains are taxed at 8.5%. Paid Family and Medical Leave payroll contributions are separate.

MI.name: Michigan

std.notes: No standard deduction.

MI.local: City income tax in 24 cities: most 1% for residents / 0.5% for nonresidents; Detroit 2.4% / 1.2%; Grand Rapids 1.5% / 0.75%.

MN.name: Minnesota

std.notes: Reduced for high-AGI filers (above roughly $239,000, by up to 80%).

exemption.notes: No personal exemption; $5,200 per dependent.

MN.notes: 1% surtax on net investment income over $1 million.

MS.name: Mississippi

exemption.notes: Another $1,500 each for 65+ or blind.

MS.notes: Rate cut from 4.7% to 4.4% for 2025, on taxable income over $10,000; 4.0% is scheduled for 2026.

MO.name: Missouri

std.notes: Equals the federal std deduction (2025 OBBBA amounts per MO DOR). Missouri does NOT allow the federal tips, overtime, car-loan-interest or senior deductions.

MO.local: 1% earnings tax in Kansas City and St. Louis on residents and on nonresidents working there.
MO.notes: Top rate cut from 4.8% to 4.7% for 2025. A 100% capital gains subtraction starts in 2025. A limited, AGI-phased deduction for federal income tax paid is allowed.

MT.name: Montana

std.notes: Federal std deduction (and Schedule 1-A deductions), already included because Montana taxable income begins with federal AGI less federal deductions; do not subtract again.

exemption.notes: No personal exemptions (a $5,660 subtraction exists for taxpayers 65+).

MT.notes: The start is federal taxable income computed without the QBI deduction. Net long-term capital gains are taxed at 3.0%/4.1%. HB 337 rate changes begin in 2026.

NE.name: Nebraska

exemption.notes: $171 credit per exemption.

NE.notes: Top rate cut from 5.84% to 5.2% for 2025.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.notes: Wages were never taxed. The Interest and Dividends Tax (3% in 2024) was repealed from Jan 1, 2025, so there is no individual income tax for 2025. Source: Tax Foundation; the NH DRA site refused the request (HTTP 403).

NJ.name: New Jersey

std.notes: No standard deduction.

NJ.local: None on individuals (Newark's 1% payroll tax is paid by employers).

NM.name: New Mexico

std.notes: Equals the federal std deduction (IRC 63), so the 2025 OBBBA amounts apply. The federal tips, overtime and senior deductions do not flow through.

exemption.notes: $4,000 deduction for each dependent except one.

NM.notes: HB 252 (2024) restructured the brackets for tax years from 2025; the top rate stays 5.9%.

NY.name: New York

exemption.notes: No personal exemption; $1,000 per dependent.

NY.local: New York City resident tax 3.078%-3.876%. Yonkers: residents pay a surcharge of 16.75% of net NYS tax; nonresidents pay 0.5% of wages earned there. MCTMT applies to self-employment income in the MTA region.
NY.notes: Tax benefit recapture: above NY AGI of $107,650 the benefit of the lower brackets is recaptured, so very high earners pay their top rate on all income. No 2025 rate change; cuts start in 2026.

NC.name: North Carolina

exemption.notes: No personal exemption. Child deduction per qualifying child by AGI: MFJ $3,000 up to $40,000, then $500 less per $20,000, $0 above $140,000. Single: $3,000 up to $20,000, then $500 less per $10,000, $0 above $70,000.

NC.notes: Rate cut from 4.5% to 4.25% for 2025; 3.99% from 2026.

ND.name: North Dakota

std.notes: Federal std deduction, already included because North Dakota starts from federal taxable income; do not subtract again. Flow-through of the 2025 OBBBA amount assumes ND's automatic IRC conformity and was not separately confirmed with the state.

ND.notes: 2025 brackets confirmed in ND's 2025 tax rate schedules.

OH.name: Ohio

std.notes: No standard deduction.

OH.local: Municipal income taxes on wages in most cities, commonly 1%-2.5% (Columbus and Cleveland 2.5%, Cincinnati 1.8%), plus school district income taxes in many districts.
OH.notes: HB 96 cut the top rate from 3.5% to 3.125% for 2025 (flat 2.75% from 2026); the Tax Foundation table shows 3.5%. The official table includes a base amount: income over $26,050 pays $342 + 2.75% of the excess, and income over $100,000 pays $2,394.32 + 3.125% of the excess. So the 0% band is lost above $26,050 and the marginal brackets alone understate tax by about $342. The joint filing credit and low-income credits are not modeled.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.notes: No 2025 change. HB 2764 cuts the top rate to 4.5% and consolidates brackets from 2026.

OR.name: Oregon

std.notes: Final 2025 DOR amounts (Tax Foundation and the 2025 estimated-tax booklet showed $2,800/$5,600).

exemption.notes: $256 credit per exemption; not allowed if federal AGI exceeds $100,000 (single) / $200,000 (joint).

OR.local: Portland Metro Supportive Housing Services tax: 1% of taxable income above $125,000 (single) / $200,000 (joint). Multnomah County Preschool for All: 1.5% above the same thresholds, plus another 1.5% above $250,000 / $400,000.
OR.notes: A subtraction for federal income tax paid (max $8,500) phases out starting at AGI $125,000 (single) / $250,000 (joint). The top bracket thresholds are not indexed. The first-bracket edges ($4,400/$8,800) are derived from DOR's published 2025 chart bases. The statewide transit tax (0.1% of wages) is withheld separately.

PA.name: Pennsylvania

std.notes: No standard deduction.

exemption.notes: No personal exemptions; a Tax Forgiveness credit applies at low incomes.

PA.local: Local earned income tax (EIT) nearly statewide, typically about 1%-2% combined municipal + school district; Pittsburgh residents 3%. Philadelphia wage tax: residents 3.75% / nonresidents 3.44% until June 30, 2025, then 3.74% / 3.43% from July 1, 2025. Many municipalities also levy a Local Services Tax (up to $52/yr).
PA.notes: Income is taxed in eight state-defined classes, not from federal AGI. No 2025 rate change.

RI.name: Rhode Island

std.notes: Phases out for modified federal AGI between $254,250 and $283,250 (none above).

exemption.notes: Same $254,250-$283,250 phase-out as the std deduction.

RI.notes: Brackets are the same for all filing statuses (indexed; 2025 values).

SC.name: South Carolina

std.notes: Federal std deduction, embedded because SC starts from federal taxable income. SC conforms to the IRC as of Dec 31, 2024, so the OBBBA increase ($750 single / $1,500 MFJ) and the federal tips/overtime/senior/car-loan deductions must be added back for 2025 (SCDOR IL 26-4).

exemption.notes: No personal exemption. $4,930 per dependent, plus another $4,930 for each dependent under age 6.

SC.notes: Top rate cut from 6.2% to 6.0% for 2025; for taxable income of $100,000 or more, tax = 6% x TI - $642. 44% of net capital gains is deductible. A major reform starts in 2026.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.notes: No individual income tax; the Hall tax on interest and dividends was fully repealed from 2021.

UT.name: Utah

std.notes: Not a deduction. The taxpayer tax credit is 6% of the federal std deduction ($15,750/$31,500 for 2025) or of federal itemized deductions excluding state income tax. The whole credit (including the dependent part) is reduced by 1.3% of income above $18,213 (single) / $36,426 (MFJ).

exemption.notes: The Utah personal exemption is $2,111 per dependent (none for taxpayer/spouse) and enters the same 6% taxpayer credit: 6% x $2,111 = $126.66 per dependent, before the phase-out.

UT.notes: HB 106 (2025) cut the rate from 4.55% to 4.5%, retroactive to Jan 1, 2025 (the Tax Foundation table shows 4.55%).

VT.name: Vermont

std.notes: Plus $1,250 for each 65+/blind box. 2025 amounts (Tax Foundation showed 2024).

VT.notes: Uses the 2025 VT rate schedules (Tax Foundation showed 2024 brackets). Minimum tax: if federal AGI exceeds $150,000, tax is the greater of the regular tax or 3% of AGI (less US obligation interest).

VA.name: Virginia

std.notes: Raised for 2025 from $8,500/$17,000. Must be used if the federal std deduction was claimed.

exemption.notes: Another $800 each for 65+ or blind.

VA.notes: Brackets are not indexed and are the same for all filing statuses.

WA.name: Washington
WA.notes: No tax on wages. A capital gains excise tax applies to long-term capital gains above a $278,000 standard deduction (2025; $270,000 in 2024). New tiered rates from tax year 2025: 7% on the first $1M of taxable gains and 9.9% above $1M. Real estate and retirement accounts are exempt. The WA Cares long-term-care premium (0.58% of wages) is a payroll deduction, not income tax.

WV.name: West Virginia

std.notes: No standard deduction.

WV.local: None (some cities charge flat weekly city service/user fees).
WV.notes: Rates cut about 4% effective Jan 1, 2025 (W. Va. Code 11-21-4i); another cut is scheduled for 2026.

WI.name: Wisconsin

std.notes: Maximum (sliding-scale) amounts that phase out as income rises. Per the Tax Foundation, the phase-out starts at about $19,549 (single) / $28,209 (MFJ) and reaches zero at about $132,549 / $155,169.

exemption.notes: Another $250 for each person 65+.

WI.notes: 2025 Act 15 widened the 4.4% bracket retroactive to Jan 1, 2025 (the Tax Foundation table shows the old $29,370/$39,150 edges). Wisconsin follows the IRC as of Dec 31, 2022.

DC.name: District of Columbia

std.notes: DC decoupled from the OBBBA increase and keeps $15,000/$30,000 for 2025. It also disallows the federal tips, overtime and senior deductions for 2025.

DC.local: None (DC itself is the local jurisdiction).
DC.notes: Brackets are the same for all filing statuses. No 2025 rate change.
